MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE HELD IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  OF THE LA VERNE CITY HALL
  Monday, February 4, 2019

1.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Kendrick at 6: 30 p. m.
2.  Council Members present:  Mayor Don Kendrick
  Mayor Pro Tem Muir Davis
  Council Member Robin Carder
  Council Member Charlie Rosales
  Council Member Tim Hepburn

  Absent:  None.

  Advisory personnel present:  City Manager Robert Russi
  City Attorney Robert L. Kress
  Assistant City Manager/ Public Works Director Dan Keesey
  Assistant City Clerk Lupe Gaeta Estrella
  Community Development Director Eric Scherer
  Community Services Director Bill Aguirre
  Police Chief Nick Paz
  Police Captain Colleen Flores
  Finance Manager Nathan Statham
  Fire Battalion Chief Robert Russell
  Personnel Officer JR Ranells

3.  Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Kendrick.

4.  Consent Calendar  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Davis, and unanimously carried to
  accept, approve, or act on the Consent Calendar items, except for the
  following:
  Council Member Carder declared a conflict of interest on Resolution
  No. 19- 02, Weed Abatement, because she is a member of the Board of
  Directors for a homeowners' association that oversees property
  appearing on the weed abatement list.

  Richard Bowen, La Verne, pulled Resolution No. 19- 03, Medical Insurance
  benefits for elected officials for further discussion.

  Registers of Audited Demands  register of Audited Demands in the amount of$ 1, 391, 620. 87, dated January
  9, 2019, in the amount of$ 733, 398. 59, dated January 16, 2019; and in the
  amount of$ 374, 229. 74, dated January 23, 2019, approved as
  recommended by staff.

  Treasurer' s Report  Treasurer' s Report for the Month of December 31, 2019, received and filed.
 City Council Minutes, Monday, February 4, 2019, Page 2

Resolution No. 19- 03,  Richard Bowen, La Verne, pulled Resolution No. 19- 03, for further discussion.
Terminating Medical Coverage  Mr. Bowen asked why the delay in bringing this matter for approval, when
for Council Pulled from the  Council approved terminating medical coverage for Council I on July 16, 2018
Consent Calendar for further  and that it would become effective December 31, 2018. He asked what had
Discussion  changed and was there a vote to extend the coverage.

  Mayor Kendrick explained that due to an ongoing illness of a Council Member,
  it was agreed to hold off until now.

  City Manager Russi also explained that at the direction of the City Council
  termination was to be December 31, 2018, only if it did not affect any medical
  coverage for a Council Member. The change of circumstances came to light
  when a Council Member with an ongoing medical need and to avoid disruption
  of care, the action to terminate was delayed.

  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Carder, and carried by a vote of 4- 1
  Davis No) to approve Resolution No. 19- 03, repealing Resolution No. 87- 18,
  regarding eligibility for medical insurance benefits for elected officials.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, February 4, 2019, Page 3

  directed staff to draft a resolution eliminating medical insurance benefits for

5.  Comprehensive Annual  City Manager Russi introduced Brad Welebir, the City' s outside independent
  Financial Report for June 30,  audit firm Rogers, Anderson, Malady & Scott, LLP ( RAMS) who was present to
  2018 Presentation  report on the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for June 30, 2018 and
  answer any questions the Council or the public may have.
  Mr. Brad Welebir, RAMS Partner reported on the Comprehensive Annual
  Financial Report for June 30, 2018. The CAFR reflects the financial position
  and operating activities of the City for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2018. He
  stated that their audit was performed in accordance with the auditing standards
  generally accepted in the United States and Governmental Auditing Standards.
  He stated that the accounting records and financial presentations are proper
  and reflect positively upon the City' s commitment to be accountable to the
  citizens concerning the City' s financial resources. The Independent Auditor's
  Report contains an unmodified opinion, which is the highest level of assurance
  that an Independent Auditor can give. He also reported that as part of the
  audit, RAMS has issued their Report on Internal Control over Financial
  Reporting and on Compliance which reports on the City' s compliance with
  certain  laws, regulation, contracts and grant agreements.  He reported there
  was no findings or deficiencies found.  He thanked Finance Manager Statham
  and City Staff for their cooperation in working with them and providing them
  with the proper documentation.

  Mayor Kendrick called for public comment on this matter.

  Richard Bowen, Eagle Drive, La Verne, stated he noticed there is a
  considerable drop in grant money over the years and asked why the huge
  decrease.

  City Manager Russi replied staff would have to do some research and get back
  to Mr. Bowen.

  Rick McGueron, 2358 Trickling Creek, asked about future retirement funding.

  City Manager Russi replied that as of today, it' s fully funded. He explained that
  CaIPERS every year determines the City' s contribution by actuarial valuation
  of the City' s liabilities, benefits and the employee groups. Currently the City is
  paying the normal cost, but it could change due to a dip in the market.

  It was moved by Rosales, seconded by Davis and unanimously approved to
  receive and file the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report, Report on
  Internal Control over Financial Reporting and on Compliance and Other
  Matters, Auditor Letter to the City Council, and the Addendum to the Annual
  Progress Report for the City' s Housing Successor Fund for the year ended
  June 30, 2018.

  The City Council thanked Finance Manager Statham and Finance staff and Mr.
  Brad Welebir, RAMS Partner for all their work on preparing the City' s audit.
 City Council Minutes, Monday, February 4, 2019, Page 4

Request Study from County of  At the January 19, 2019 Council meeting, Mayor Pro Tem Davis asked for an
Los Angeles Regarding Fire  agenda item requesting Los Angeles County to conduct a feasibility study for
Services  providing fire services be placed on the agenda for discussion.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis stated that he felt that with the City making good
  headway on years 1 and 2 efforts identified in the Fiscal Sustainability Plan,
  that he thought this would be a good time to bring this matter forward, since it
  would take a long time to study.

  Council Member Carder stated she did not support doing the study. She said
  she promised her constituents when she ran for Council that she would keep
  our City services. She stated that if the City Council does agree to conduct a
  fire service feasibility study, she would like the following addressed in the
  specifications.

  Compare apples to apples
  Same or better response times
  Same transport arrival time to facility

  She stated that it' s a different outcome for a 3 minutes response time vs a 71/ 2
  minutes response as quoted by former Fire Chief Breaux.

  Council Member Carder reported that unfortunately the County has the City at
  a disadvantage since the County knows what the City pays for fire personnel
  and services; and it would make it easier for them to give the City a lower
  quote; and later raise the cost in the later years. She stated she would like the
  following addressed.

  Find out what the percentage the increases would be.
  Proposal should include 5- 7 cities that have gone from city to county and
  also those who have gone from county to city.

  Council Member Hepburn agreed with Council Member Carder. He stated he
  would support a fire feasibility study if the citizens want it. He said he was
  happy with the Fire Department and their services. He stated he was not
  opposed to a free study, but only if the citizens want it. He stated he was
  concerned about how this would affect the lawsuits. He did not want to irritate
  the situation. He just wanted to avoid another lawsuit.

  Council Member Rosales stated that the paramedic unit would not be part of
  the study. He stated he was in favor in doing a preliminary study to explore
  the matter.

  City Attorney Kress stated that the Fire Association has brought this matter to
  Council in the past, but the City would have to ask the Fire Association how
  they feel about it now.
  Mayor called for public comment on this matter.

  Ed Venegas, 7152 Via Dicha, La Verne, stated that the City should have a side
  bar discussion with the Fire Association to see if their position was has
  changed and see want they want.

  Rick McGueron, 2358 Trickling Creek, La Verne, stated the City needs to ask
  the Fire Association what their position regarding conducting the study.
 City Council Minutes, Monday. February 4, 2019, Page 5

  Dennis Navarre, 4573 Derby Circle, La Verne asked who would do the study
  and would it be with the County of Los Angeles.

  Pam Berry, La Verne, stated that she was really confused about where the
  Council stood regarding conducting a feasibility fire study. She stated that in
  the past Council Member Carder and Mayor Pro Tern Davis did not support
  conducting a fire feasibility study. She referred to the February minutes, where
  Council Member Carder stated that she did not support contracting with the
  County of Los Angeles for fire services and that that matter was final and not
  to be revisited. She also stated that the majority of the Council agreed. She
  asked what has changed their mind and what was the reason for bringing this
  matter back.

  Ed Venegas, 152 Via Dicha, La Verne, asked who the City' s parliamentarian is
  and what are the rules that allow Council City to bring this matter back for
  discussion. He asked if the City followed the Robert' s Rules of Order.

  City Attorney Kress replied that the City of La Verne has not adopted the
  Robert' s Rules of Order.

  Mayor Kendrick stated that the City Council at its last meeting adopted rules so
  that the prevailing party can bring back an item back to Council. According to
  the rules. Council Members Carder and Rosales, and Mayor Pro Tern Davis,
  and he had the right to bring the matter back to Council.

  City Manager Russi informed Mr. Venegas, he would email him a copy of the
  rules.

  Rick McGueron, 2318 Trickling Creek, La Verne, stated that apparently the
  Council can vote not to ever consider a matter ever again and later one person
  can decide to bring back the matter. He stated how the residents were
  supposed to have confidence and faith in the Council' s vote, if they later
  changed their minds.

  City Attorney Kress explained that the recent City of San Gabriel Fire study
  was shared with the City Council. The study showed that the City would
  experience a savings by contracting with County and that both cities were
  similar in size.

  Jim Murphy, 4940 Raymond Drive, La Verne, stated that the missing piece
  was the cost to do the feasibility study that was discussed at the February
  meeting and that is why it was stated it would not be brought back to Council.
  He stated he would be interested to see what was in the study, especially if it
  addressed response time.

  Mayor Pro Tern Davis stated that last year. Council Member Carder did not
  support conducting a fire study along with the majority of the Council, but he
  felt it was a good time to bring this forward when this new information was
  made available and with the City making good headway with the fiscal
  sustainability plan. He felt that this matter had not died away.

  Aryn Plax, 1950 Third Street, La Verne and University of La Verne student,
  stated she has kept up with this matter since last year and she noted that one
  of the citizen' s concerns was response time. She asked if the City Council
  was concerned with the amount of personnel that would be available if the City
  contracts with the County and fire standards.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, February 4, 2019, Page 6

  Mayor Kendrick stated that the City has the best paramedic service in the
  area. He explained that the City of La Verne Fire Department also has the
  support of Los Angeles County Fire Department resources, if needed.

  Richard Bowen, Eagle Drive, La Verne, stated he agreed with Mr. Murphy, that
  a year ago, the reason that the matter was tabled was the cost associated in
  conducting the study. He stated that if the study is free, Council should do it
  and find out what the County has to offer.

  There were no more public comments from the floor.

  Council Member Hepburn stated he wanted to be safe and wait before doing
  free study. He stated that City should do their due diligence, because he did
  not want more lawsuits. He felt that this is a sensative matter and was
  concerned with what would be left after the lawsuits are settled.

  City Manager Russi suggested that Council can direct him to email the Fire
  Association President for his input and where the Association stood on the
  study.

  Council Member Rosales stated that he vacillated over the pro and cons of
  contracting with the County of Los Angeles Fire Department. He stated that
  the two agencies are not the same. He stated that Los Angeles County Fire
  Department will not keep our fire personnel and that positions are assigned by
  seniority. He stated he supported doing the study, but the City should contact
  the Fire Association to see how they stood on matter. He said he did not want
  unhappy employees. He stated that the City of La Verne is a great place work.

  Council Member Carder stated that she did not want to contract with County.
  She felt that that County would come in with low quote for fire services just to
  get La Verne and in later years the cost for services will go up. She stated she
  loves the City' s Fire Department; they are top notch and she did not want to
  lose the current La Verne fire personnel. She said the mobile home parks love
  the Fire Department. She stated again, that she did not support the doing the
  study.

  Mayor Kendrick stated he was not against doing the study, but was against
  contracting with the County of Los Angeles for fire services. He stated that
  La Verne has the best in the industry. He spoke about how the City of Pomona
  is not happy that they went County. He stated that La Verne residents love
  having their own fire department and the Council represents the residents.

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Rosales to conduct a feasibility study for
  providing fire services. Not approved by a vote of 2-3, Rosales and Davis
  voted Yes, and Kendrick, Carder and Hepburn voted No.

7.  Public Comment  This was the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City Council on
  items not listed in any other place on the agenda. Mayor Kendrick called for
  public comment.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, February 4, 2019, Page 7

  George Henderson, Old Town La Verne, addressed the City Council regarding
  Sierra La Verne Golf Course. He stated that they met with the owner and were
  informed that they will be doing an assessment on whether to keep the Sierra
  La Verne Golf Course private or public. He stated that the City needs to be pro-
  active and a game plan is needed to deal with the owner and his plans. He
  suggested ways the Council can deter the owner from closing the golf course or
  going public by insisting that grounds be maintained so not to create a fire
  hazard; look at the Federal law regarding migration of birds, look at the
  dependency of wildlife on the golf course, oak trees offenses, and use other
  public agencies, like Peta to help the fight. He said that a water deal with the
  owner is good idea. He also suggested the City form a committee to discuss
  strategies. He stated many community members wished to keep the golf course
  private.

  Dennis Navarre, 4573 Derby Circle, La Verne, also spoke about Sierra
  La Verne Golf Course. He stated that the golf course is a disaster and it' s a
  liability.

  Rick McGueron, 2358 Trickling Lane, La Verne, also spoke about Sierra
  La Verne Golf Course. He said he' s not a golfer, but it still concerns him. He
  suggested that the City Council get in front of this matter as they did with
  Marshall Canyon.

  Orlando Jackson, 3970 Turquoise Lane, La Verne, stated he wanted to bring
  awareness of profiling in the City. He stated he is a disabled US Army Veteran
  with twenty- one years of active honorable service and earned a purple heart.
  He spoke at length about his life and dealing with profiling in his own country.
  He spoke about an incident involving the La Verne Police Department
  detaining him because of allegations that he shoplifted and also spoke of two
  other incidents in La Verne. He stated he loves La Verne and he is a member
  of the VFW. He wished people could be more open- minded and that his skin
  should not be his sin.

  Dennis Navarre, 4573 Derby Circle, La Verne, spoke about an incident in
  which he was in a funeral procession with his ceremonial rifle to honor a fallen
  veteran, when a citizen called the police on him because of the rifle. He stated
  that it happens to good and honest people. He stated he respects Mr. Orlando
  Jackson and thanked him for his service.

  Thomas Allison, 4515 Ramona, wished the City Council Happy Black History
  Month. He also spoke at length about awareness and profiling. He urged the
  City Council for more action and discussion to see more diversity. He
  suggested a human relations' committee be formed to address profiling and
  awareness in the Community.

8.  Council Comments and  Council Member Hepburn thanked and recognized all the first responders and
  Meeting/ Conference Reports  thanked everyone for attending.

  Mayor Pro Tem Davis thanked Thomas Allison for coming and also wished him
  Happy Black History Month and hopefully, we have learned from history and
  can move forward.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, February 4, 2019, Page 8

  Council Member Carder reported on the Gold Line meeting she attended and
  that the Gold Line terminus will be extended to Pomona. She also reported on
  the grant money given to Tri- City Mental Health Authority, which will be
  beneficial for the La Verne Police who will have a homeless navigator available
  at all times.

  Council member Rosales thanked Orlando Jackson for his service to our
  Country.

  Mayor Kendrick also thanked Thomas Allison and Orlando Jackson for their
  attendance and he stated that as a nation, we should do better. He said that
  tonight' s topic on awareness of profiling is very important.

9.  Adjournment to Tuesday, February 19, 2019, at 4: 30 pm, fora Council Study Session on Committees in the
  Conference Room of City Hall.

  Due to the City Hall being closed on Monday, February 18, 2019, in observance of a legal holiday, THE NEXT
  REGULAR  MEETING of the La Verne City Council was scheduled for Tuesday, February 19, 2019, at 6: 30 pm.

  Respectfully submitted,
